claims.text: The untreated Ti-6Al-4V has a homogeneous microstructure and baseline surface properties typical of the alloy.
The proposed intervention is laser cladding a preplaced mixture of WC and titanium-alloy powder onto Ti-6Al-4V.
The laser cladding is to be performed under argon at a laser power of 1–2 kW and a controlled scan speed.
In situ monitoring and post-cladding homogenization will promote uniform formation and distribution of reaction products.
Laser cladding will produce a composite laser-remelted surface layer.
The composite layer will contain TiC formed in situ.
The composite layer will contain retained WC particles.
TiC and retained WC will be evenly distributed through the clad layer.
Rapid melting and solidification during laser cladding triggers reactions between titanium and the WC-containing powder.
The reaction between titanium and the WC-containing powder forms TiC.
TiC and retained WC particles impart dispersion strengthening to the surface layer.
Dispersion strengthening increases the surface layer's resistance to plastic deformation.
Increased resistance to plastic deformation enhances surface hardness and wear resistance.
The treated surface will exhibit an approximately 30–40% increase in microhardness relative to untreated Ti-6Al-4V.
The treated surface will exhibit a significant reduction in sliding wear rate relative to untreated Ti-6Al-4V.
The predicted improvement depends on obtaining a uniform phase distribution and robust interface bonding.
The hardness and wear improvements are expected under sliding wear at room temperature and moderately elevated temperatures around 200°C.
Deviations from the selected processing parameters or failure to obtain uniform phases may negate the expected improvements.
